actual_model_identity: Not independently exposed by runtime tools; agent was assigned as GPT-6 Astra reviewer 2.
claimed_surface: Bounded independent correctness review of typed SELECT renderer, parameter transport, exact output names/types/modifiers/collations, source parsing versus canonical structure, and test provenance.
No full PostgreSQL release approval; StaticValid excludes execution, cardinality, literal conversion and recursive termination.

attempts.result: 241 contract-valid cases and one parser rejection. Native source and canonical gdesc agreed for all admitted cases. Compared exact names/types/modifiers and collations against contract: one concrete signed-boundary mismatch, reduced separately. 233 valid native temporary-view descriptors permitted catalog collation comparison; eight indeterminate-collation FULL JOIN outputs cannot be persisted as view columns, while source/canonical gdesc succeeded and contract reported null collation.

Independently authored signed literal tests around 2^31 and 2^63, repeated minus, unary plus, parentheses, cast and scalar-subquery barriers, array/CTE/arithmetic/UNION composition. Ten exact-type discrepancies from the same incomplete raw-literal folding rule. Source and canonical native descriptors agree. Bare double-negative values execute successfully as positive bigint/numeric values. Explicit cast and scalar-subquery barriers retain the narrower native types and agree with the contract.

Inspected lexical/AST parameter traversal, binding map and transport, renderer ambiguities, fixed corpus hashes/count assertions, source-only nonexecution guards, and separate PREPARE/gdesc/execution paths. No additional concrete issue established; did not execute source corpus SQL or DDL.

objections.claim: Repeated raw unary minus on an integer boundary is typed by recursively assigning the inner minimum signed integer and then preserving that narrow type. PostgreSQL folds the entire raw minus-literal chain before selecting its type. Thus an admitted result can have a different native type from its exact output contract. The same issue is in normative OrdinaryUnary/ExprValid rules, not only the checker.

reproducer.native: SELECT -(-2147483648) followed by psql \gdesc; repeat canonical SELECT (-(-2147483648));
additional_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT -(-2147483648) AS n) SELECT n FROM c

objections.expected: Native original and canonical output descriptor ?column?|bigint; value 2147483648. At 2^63 the output type is numeric and value 9223372036854775808. The contract must match native types or return Unsupported, rather than Valid with int32/bigint respectively.
objections.actual: status valid, typePrecision exact, outputColumns [{name:"?column?",nullable:false,type:"int32"}], outputCollations [null]; 2^63 case reports bigint, array case integer[] instead of bigint[]. Native source/canonical both analyze and the bare positive boundary result executes successfully, so this is not a runtime-overflow exclusion.
